title: Security & Data-Protection Request Decision Matrix and SLA Tiers
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable, auditable decision matrix and corresponding SLA tiers for inbound enterprise security and data-protection asks (SOC2/ISO evidence requests, HIPAA/DPA contractual clauses, GDPR data subject flows, and vendor questionnaires).

Scope: This work covers non-bug customer requests that currently route to PM/Support/Legal/Security for manual triage. Deliverables include a decision matrix (severity, required responder, required artifacts, expected turnaround), three SLA tiers (Standard/Accelerated/Legal Escalation) with measurable SLAs, routing rules for the intake system, and a set of templated responses and artifact checklists to reduce manual overhead.

Why now: Increased enterprise adoption has led to a 55% YoY increase in questionnaire and DPA asks. Our existing ad-hoc triage causes inconsistent turnaround, missed SLAs in renewals, and friction in sales cycles. A lightweight, policy-driven decision matrix will reduce manual handoffs and accelerate responses while documenting risk boundaries for legal/security.

Stakeholders: Security (lead: Priya Kapoor), Legal (lead: Daniel Morales), Sales Ops (lead: Jenna Park), Customer Success (lead: Omar Reyes), Engineering (infra/console owners), and Solutions Engineering.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Decision matrix drafted and reviewed by Security + Legal; 2) Three SLA tiers defined with target TATs and SLA metrics; 3) Routing rules documented and configured in intake playbook (Support <> PM <> Security <> Legal); 4) 5 templated artifact bundles (SOC2 summary, ISO cert extract, DPA clause template, HIPAA control matrix, GDPR DSAR checklist) produced as docs and linked in the intake system; 5) Pilot with two enterprise customers and measurable improvement in turnaround (target 40% reduction in median TAT).

Proposed plan: Week 0–1: interviews with Security/Legal/Sales Ops to capture current ask types and historical TATs; Week 2: draft matrix and SLA tiers, produce artifact templates; Week 3: review cycle with stakeholders and iterate; Week 4: pilot automation/routing in intake and run two live pilots; Week 5: incorporate feedback and finalize playbook.

Risks/assumptions: R1: Legal review cycles can add days; mitigate with pre-approved clause templates and a Legal escalation lane. R2: Some customers will request bespoke contractual language; these should map to the Legal Escalation SLA and be explicitly excluded from Standard/Accelerated SLA promises. R3: Engineering work to surface templated artifacts in the console may require a small UI task—estimate 3 engineering days (ENG-2011).

Open questions: Q1: Should certain high-value customers get a bespoke SLA tier outside the standard matrix? Q2: How will we log and audit acceptance of templates to support future SOC2/ISO audits? Q3: What metrics will count as SLA violations (first substantive response vs full closure)?

Artifacts / links: - Intake spreadsheet with historic asks (drive link): https://drive.company/reports/enterprise-intake-history - Draft matrix doc (confluence): https://confluence.company/pm/security-decision-matrix - Template artifacts folder (drive): https://drive.company/compliance/templates - Related Linear ticket for implementation: ENG-2011

Next steps (this ticket): 1) Run stakeholder interviews and upload notes to confluence (assignee: Marco); 2) Produce first-pass matrix and SLA table for Security/legal review by 2025-01-24; 3) Prepare 5 artifact templates for pilot by 2025-02-07.
